why: Population Source binding digest vectors, produced by an implementation that is NOT the code under test. packages/domain/src/sources/population-source.ts is checked against these bytes; a fixture produced by that module would prove only that it equals itself. The envelopes in the generator are written out by hand, so the projection from a binding to its five hashed keys is checked too, not just the hash of an envelope this repository derived.
algorithm: digest = SHA-256( RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the five-key envelope {declared_count_mechanism, declared_schema, kind, location, sensitive_fields} ), lower-case hex. declared_schema keeps its typed order; sensitive_fields is sorted by UTF-16 code unit.

vectors.name: versioned-file-cover-sheet
vectors.note: A versioned file whose expected count comes from a signed cover sheet. The declared schema keeps the order it was typed in — it is a positional declaration — while the sensitive fields are sorted, because masking is a membership question. Both lists are given here with a duplicate and a blank, and both drop them.

vectors.name: read-only-api-count-endpoint
vectors.note: A read-only API whose expected count comes from a count endpoint, with no sensitive field designated. Every key is still present: an absent value is an empty list, never a missing key.

vectors.name: manual-upload-no-location
vectors.note: A manual upload names nowhere: the file arrives with the Run. The location slot is null rather than absent, so this kind produces the same five keys as every other. A location typed anyway is dropped, which is why one is given here.

vectors.name: schema-order-reversed
vectors.note: Byte-identical to the first vector except that two schema fields are swapped. Its digest must differ: the declared schema is ordered, and a parser told the other order would read the wrong column.

vectors.name: sensitive-fields-order-irrelevant
vectors.note: Byte-identical to the first vector except that the sensitive fields are typed in the other order. Its digest must EQUAL the first vector's: they are a set. This is the vector that fails if sensitive_fields is ever hashed as a list.

vectors.name: unicode-field-names
vectors.note: Multi-byte UTF-8 field names and location. RFC 8785 sorts object keys by UTF-16 code unit and emits the characters unescaped, and the domain module sorts the sensitive-field set the same way. The U+FFFD sentinel is what makes that testable: it sorts AFTER the astral-plane emoji by UTF-16 code unit (0xD83D, the emoji's leading surrogate, is below 0xFFFD) and BEFORE it by code point (U+FFFD < U+1F50E), so a code-point comparator fails this vector.
